title: xgames-kit shared definitions
description: Definitions every other schema refers to. The $id is a name, not a URL that resolves: load every schema through registry/schemas.mjs.

id.description: A registry id: lower case, digits and dashes. Runtimes, profiles (2d, flat-2d), loops, mechanics, kinds, worlds, looks and camera rigs all use it.

assetRef.description: An asset in the library: <pack id>/<asset id>.

path.description: A path relative to the repository root (or, inside a game, to the game's folder). Never absolute, never climbing out with ../.

evidence.description: One piece of proof: a file in the repository (an evidence folder, a verdict.json, a test) or an outside record, with the day it was made.

what.description: What it shows, in plain words.

browser.description: For a device claim: the browser and version it ran in.

hardware.description: For a device claim: the hardware class (e.g. 'desktop, discrete GPU', 'phone emulated in headless Chrome').

state.description: Three separate facts (DESIGN 'Adding a runtime, a mechanic or a kind'). exists: it is in code. tested: it passed its tests, with evidence. open: a pitch may offer it. open needs exists; tested needs evidence. A thing that does not exist is never open.

device.description: Where a game is played. x-post: inside a post on X (a sandboxed frame with no pointer lock, 480x480 at the smallest). A claim about one names the browser and hardware it was tested on (state evidence).

jsonSchema.description: A JSON Schema (2020-12) object. Its own validity is checked by the tool that compiles it, not here.

spdx.description: An SPDX id (MIT, CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, Apache-2.0), or LicenseRef-<name> for our own or a paid licence.

file.description: The licence text beside the code or the pack.

credit.description: The credit line a game must carry (CC-BY and the like).

slotTemplate.description: A gf-assets/1 slot template (CONTRACT §2.2): id may hold {base}, {i}, {id}, {as} and {<param>}; the rest is the slot as gf-assets/1 defines it.

capability.description: Something a runtime profile can do that an idea may need (registry/capabilities.json lists them: characters, voxel-world, tilemap, photoreal-water, …). What no profile has is built in the game.

fidelity.description: How far the picture goes, as a hard limit: standard (toon, low-poly, flat 2D), stylised-scenic (painterly light, living grass, fog, a day cycle), photoreal (physical sky, simulated sea).

buildId.description: A build promise: build.<n>, the spec's build[n-1].
